heading: At a Friend's Table
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Basic Manners – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 18–21.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Basic Manners (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

reading.title: How to Be a Great Guest

paras.label: A
paras.text: Every family has its own way of doing things, and their habits may be quite different from what you {are used to|are used to}. This is natural, because people come from different countries and {cultures|cultures}. Your family might always eat spaghetti on Sundays, while your friend's family might prefer fried rice, pickled beetroot or strudel.

paras.label: B
paras.text: So what should you do if you are {invited|invited} to dinner and the food on the table is completely new to you? The answer is simple: give it a try. You might {discover|discover} a new favourite. Even dishes that sound strange, like fried frog legs or pickled pig's feet, could turn out to be delicious! {Pulling a face|pulling a face} or asking for something else would be unkind to the people who cooked for you.

paras.label: C
paras.text: {Customs|customs} vary around the world. In Japan, for instance, children often {bow|bow} when they arrive at someone's house for dinner. Noticing and respecting these differences is part of being a good guest.

paras.label: D
paras.text: One final piece of advice: don't be a {slob|slob}. Clean up after yourself. If you have been finger painting at school, wash your hands instead of wearing the paint home. And after eating at a friend's house, offer to carry your dishes to the sink.

paras.label: E
paras.text: Good manners make everyone feel comfortable. They help us make friends and even {solve|solve} problems. Keep practising them, and you may become the best-liked kid in town.

parts.title: Part 1 · Which paragraph?
parts.instr: Đoạn nào (A–E) chứa thông tin dưới đây?

items.label: A paragraph that says each family's habits can be different
items.why: Đoạn A: *Every family has its own way of doing things.*

items.label: A paragraph that explains what to do if you don't recognise the food
A paragraph that gives an example of a greeting custom in another country
items.why: Đoạn C: trẻ em Nhật cúi chào.

items.label: A paragraph that describes habits of a tidy person
items.why: Đoạn D: rửa tay, mang bát đĩa ra bồn rửa.

items.label: A paragraph that mentions manners helping to solve problems
items.why: Đoạn E: *help us make friends and even solve problems.*

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: According to paragraph A, why do families have different habits?
options: People come from different countries and cultures.
Children choose the food at home.
Shops sell different food every day.
questions.why: *…because people come from different countries and cultures.*

questions.q: The writer suggests asking for a different meal if you don't like the look of the food.
questions.why: Sai. Đoạn B: hỏi món khác là *unkind*.

questions.q: Why does the writer mention frog legs and pig's feet?
options: as examples of food that sounds strange but may taste good
to show what Japanese children eat
because they are the writer's favourite dishes
to warn readers not to eat them
questions.why: *…dishes that sound strange… could turn out to be delicious!*

questions.q: In paragraph C, bowing in Japan is an example of…
questions.why: *Customs vary around the world. In Japan, for instance…*

questions.q: The writer says good manners can help people get on with each other.
questions.why: Đúng. Đoạn E: *help us make friends and even solve problems.*

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the text?
options: to give advice on being a polite guest and respecting differences
to teach readers how to cook new dishes
to compare food in Japan and South America
to explain how to finger paint
questions.why: Cả bài là lời khuyên khi làm khách và tôn trọng sự khác biệt.

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: The girls are trying food at a friend's house. Which advice are they following?
questions.why: Họ đang nếm thử món ăn – đúng lời khuyên *give it a try* (đoạn B).
questions.alt: Two girls at a table, each holding a meatball on a fork

options: carrying his dishes to the sink after the meal
questions.why: Đúng lời khuyên cuối đoạn D.
questions.alt: A boy carrying his plate to a woman standing by the kitchen sink

questions.q: Which word from the text is the OPPOSITE of how the boy is behaving?
questions.why: **Slob** = người bừa bộn, không dọn dẹp – ngược với cậu bé.
questions.alt: A boy carrying his plate to a woman standing by the kitchen sink

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: When I stayed with my friend Mai's family, they served a fish soup I had never tasted before. [1] I took a small spoonful and, to my surprise, I loved it. [2] After dinner, I helped carry the bowls to the kitchen. [3]
options: At first, I was a little worried because it smelled very strong.
Mai's grandmother laughed and gave me a second bowl.
Her mum said I was one of the most polite guests they'd ever had.
I told them that my mum's soup was much better.
Then I ordered a pizza on my phone.

items.why: Lo lắng ban đầu → câu sau *to my surprise, I loved it* tạo đối lập.
Thích món ăn → bà cho thêm bát nữa.
Giúp dọn bát → mẹ Mai khen là khách lịch sự.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *Pulling a face… would be unkind* (B). **Pull a face** means…
options: make an expression that shows you don't like something
draw a picture of a face
questions.why: **Pull a face** = nhăn mặt tỏ ý không thích.

questions.q: *…different from what you are used to* (A). **Be used to something** means…
options: use it every day at school

questions.q: *…don't be a slob. Clean up after yourself.* (D). A **slob** is a person who…
questions.why: Câu sau *Clean up after yourself* giúp đoán nghĩa: người bừa bộn.
